about.title: San Ramon Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in San Ramon follows a crash, a fall, or another preventable event, the paperwork arrives long before the grief settles. San Ramon's public crash records for 2025 show 134 injury collisions, 185 people hurt, and one life lost. California treats a wrongful death claim as a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal investigation or traffic citation. The right to bring that claim belongs first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. Most families have two years from the date of death to act, and far less if a public agency such as a city or transit district is involved. The losses the law recognizes are concrete: funeral and burial expenses, the income the household counted on, and the companionship and guidance that cannot be replaced. LawProactive is free and is not a law firm. We simply connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you can ask questions without adding a bill to an already heavy month.

items.question: My family member was killed on I-680 in San Ramon. Does it matter that it was a state freeway?
items.answer: It can. If any part of the claim involves a public entity such as Caltrans, California requires a formal government claim within a much shorter period than the usual two years. The same is true if a city or county road condition on Bollinger Canyon Road or Crow Canyon Road played a role. An attorney can determine quickly whether that shorter deadline applies to you.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that proceeds separately from any criminal prosecution in Contra Costa County. The criminal case addresses punishment, while the civil claim addresses your family's losses. Waiting for a verdict could put you up against the filing deadline.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: The law recognizes funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Each family's circumstances differ, so no one can tell you a figure in advance. An independent attorney can walk through what applies to your situation.
